title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 47
paragraphs: Xerxes answered: “Artabanus, of human life, which is as you define it, let us stop speaking — and let us not remember evils when we have good things in hand. But tell me this: if the vision of the dream had not appeared to you with such clarity, would you still be holding to your former opinion and trying to stop me from marching against Greece, or would you have changed? Come, tell me exactly.” He replied: “O king, may the vision of the dream that appeared have the fulfillment that we both desire! But I am still to this moment full of dread and cannot contain myself, when I consider many things, and especially when I see that two things, which are the greatest of all, are utterly hostile to you.”
